methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Cabinet secretary: Southside county loses two economic development prospects due to uncertainty over data center taxes
signals.signal_reading: Tax uncertainty causes Greensville County to lose data center opportunities, revealing how policy instability prevents even shallow AI infrastructure investment from reaching historically underserved regions, reinforcing concentration in established metros.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-backed community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia signals potential for distributed, deep capability building through local institutions, though success depends on whether training produces genuine AI fluency or credential theater.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership concentrates institutional resources and expertise in Richmond metro, potentially deepening capability in a second hub but offering no mechanism for knowledge distribution to rural regions.

signals.title: Kennedy: NextEra-Dominion’s AI future could reshape Virginia’s economy — and its energy politics
signals.signal_reading: NextEra-Dominion deal reshapes energy infrastructure 'from Northern Virginia to Wise and Halifax counties' for AI demands, but infrastructure presence doesn't equal capability distribution—likely reinforces metro concentration while exporting costs.

signals.title: U.Va. pilots three new artificial intelligence literacy courses - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: UVA's three AI literacy courses signal platform-based, shallow adoption model being institutionalized at scale—broad exposure without deep fluency, potentially creating distributed surface-level familiarity rather than technical capability.
